hook: Turn the date. Move around Earth. Watch the real sky answer.
outcome: Explore daily and seasonal sky patterns, lunar phases, stellar brightness and the observer's place on Earth.
sources: Yale Bright Star Catalogue, Hoffleit and Warren 1991. Public domain / US Government Works per https://data.nasa.gov/dataset/bright-star-catalog. Full HEASARC file https://heasarc.gsfc.nasa.gov/FTP/heasarc/dbase/tdat_files/heasarc_bsc5p.tdat.gz; independently maintained CDS/CfA comparison https://vizier.cfa.harvard.edu/viz-bin/VizieR?-source=V/50. 9096 stellar rows, all 8786 measured B-V values, RA, DEC, Vmag, proper motion, spectral class and flags. Fetched 2026-11-05.

IAU WGSN Catalog of Star Names, 2022-04-04 snapshot, 333 HR-matched names retained and checked against fresh raw file. Creative Commons Attribution, exact version unspecified in header. https://github.com/mirandadam/iau-starnames/blob/master/catalog_data/IAU-CSN.txt. Fetched 2026-11-05.

Olaf Frohn, d3-celestial constellation lines, BSD 3-Clause, the explicit spec fallback. https://github.com/ofrohn/d3-celestial/blob/master/data/constellations.lines.json. Converted coordinates to Yale HR paths for all 88 figures; 893 endpoints checked against Yale. Full licence embedded in Manual. IAU reference identities and CC BY 4.0 chart terms: https://www.iau.org/IAU/Astronomy-FAQs/Constellations.aspx. Fetched 2026-11-05. IAU archive unavailable; no claim of an exact new chart tracing.

Natural Earth 1:50m populated places, public domain https://www.naturalearthdata.com/about/terms-of-use/. Official raw archive https://naciscdn.org/naturalearth/50m/cultural/ne_50m_populated_places_simple.zip and maintained data https://github.com/nvkelso/natural-earth-vector/blob/master/geojson/ne_50m_populated_places.geojson. 1238 of 1251 entries retained after coordinate checks; 13 unverified/conflicting entries omitted. Native TIMEZONE fields provide home-zone associations. Fetched 2026-11-05.

Wikidata P625 coordinate facts, CC0 https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Wikidata:Licensing. Independent verification of the 1238 retained Natural Earth centres within 0.25 degrees. No prose or images reproduced. API raw records and per-place differences preserved in Scratch, fetched 2026-11-05.

NASA HEASARC Messier Nebulae, Hirshfeld and Sinnott 1985; public domain / US Government Works per https://data.nasa.gov/dataset/messier-nebulae; numerical factual positions, magnitudes and identifiers only, no protected presentation or text. https://heasarc.gsfc.nasa.gov/W3Browse/general-catalog/messier.html. Twenty lowest-magnitude entries cross-checked against Hartmut Frommert and Christine Kronberg, SEDS http://messier.seds.org/data.html. Source magnitude disagreements appear as ranges; M41 centres differ by 14 arcminutes within its extent. No outside images or prose are redistributed. Fetched 2026-11-05.

NASA fact-page distance fallback, public-domain factual numbers only; no ESA catalogue redistribution (ESA states CC BY-NC 3.0 IGO at https://www.cosmos.esa.int/web/hipparcos/catalogues). 14 checked stellar distances. Primary and second-source records in _scratch/sky-dome/data/second/distance-checks.json. Sirius https://science.nasa.gov/asset/hubble/the-dog-star-sirius-and-its-tiny-companion/; Vega https://www.nasa.gov/missions/dart/nasas-dart-captures-one-of-night-skys-brightest-stars/ and https://science.nasa.gov/photojournal/tiny-particles-so-far-away/; nearby stars https://imagine.gsfc.nasa.gov/features/cosmic/solar_neighborhood_info.html; Altair https://science.nasa.gov/image-article/apod-2015-june-27-stars-of-a-summer-triangle/; Arcturus https://science.nasa.gov/resource/whats-up-june-2023-skywatching-tips-from-nasa/; Castor and Pollux https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/skywatching/night-sky-network/gemini-constellation/; Capella https://science.nasa.gov/image-article/apod-2021-february-6-a-northern-winter-night/; Alpha Centauri https://science.nasa.gov/missions/hubble/hubbles-best-image-of-alpha-centauri-a-and-b/; Fomalhaut https://science.nasa.gov/missions/hubble/hubble-directly-observes-a-planet-orbiting-another-star/; Betelgeuse https://science.nasa.gov/missions/hubble/nasa-hubble-helps-detect-wake-of-betelgeuses-elusive-companion-star/. Retrieved 2026-11-05.

JPL Standish and Williams, Approximate Positions of the Planets, numerical facts and independent implementation, https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/planets/approx_pos.html. All five planets independently compared against JPL Horizons DE441 at 2026-11-05 00:00 UTC. Raw Horizons responses in Scratch, fetched 2026-11-05.

Jean Meeus, Astronomical Algorithms. Independently written mathematical methods for precession, Sun, Moon, sidereal time and horizon events. No book text or code reproduced. USNO reference https://aa.usno.navy.mil/data/RS_OneDay and NASA factual references for sidereal rotation, Polaris and lunar motion.

F. J. Ballesteros, New insights into black bodies (2012), https://arxiv.org/abs/1201.1809. Independent implementation of mathematical colour-temperature formula; no paper text, figures or code reproduced. A display-colour approximation, not a measured spectrum.

IAU licensing clarification checked 2026-11-05: the retained name snapshot states Creative Commons Attribution without a version; the current IAU web-text policy specifies CC BY 4.0 at https://www.iau.org/IAU/Iau/Copyright.aspx and https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. IAU WGSN credited and snapshot selection disclosed in the Manual.

US Naval Observatory fresh reference calculations retrieved 2026-11-05: https://aa.usno.navy.mil/data/RS_OneDay and https://aa.usno.navy.mil/data/MoonPhases. US Government Works / public-domain numerical facts. Denver solstices and three November 2026 lunar phases compared in _scratch/sky-dome/review-numbers.json; raw responses and exact API URLs in _scratch/sky-dome/data/review/manifest.json.

Discovery-note factual paraphrases: USNO sidereal time https://aa.usno.navy.mil/faq/GAST; NASA North Star https://science.nasa.gov/solar-system/what-is-the-north-star-and-how-do-you-find-it/; NASA Moon motion https://www.nasa.gov/solar-system/why-can-you-see-the-moon-during-the-day-we-asked-a-nasa-scientist-episode-19/; NASA Goddard Venus geometry https://pwg.gsfc.nasa.gov/stargaze/Skepler3(op).htm. US Government Works / public-domain factual material; original paraphrases and mathematical implementations, no source prose or images reproduced. Verified 2026-11-05.

Geographic correction, verified 2026-11-05: Natural Earth NE_ID 1159149391 has conflicting NAME Niamey and NAMEASCII Maradi. Its Wikidata identifier https://www.wikidata.org/wiki/Q664550 confirms Maradi. The corrected name and regenerated zone indexes preserve Niamey at its separate source record Q3674. Natural Earth public domain; Wikidata CC0. Reproducible packer _scratch/sky-dome/review_pack.py.

NASA Goddard Thuban reference https://svs.gsfc.nasa.gov/13512 and NASA APOD Mars retrograde explanation https://science.nasa.gov/image-article/apod-2018-november-8-mars-in-the-loop/. Original factual paraphrases only, no source prose, photographs or videos bundled. US Government factual material. Checked 2026-11-05.

Magnitude scale: NASA Marshall / Chandra https://wwwastro.msfc.nasa.gov/solar/chandra101/variable_stars/mag.html and NASA Space Math https://spacemath.gsfc.nasa.gov/news/6Page135.pdf. US Government factual material; original explanation only, no source prose or images reproduced. Five magnitude units mean a factor of 100 in received light. Checked 2026-11-05.

NASA Goddard Sun Fact Sheet, David R. Williams: https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/sunfact.html. Nominal visual magnitude -26.74, explicitly identified as nominal rather than date-dependent in the readout and Manual. US Government factual numerical material; no source prose or art reproduced. Checked 2026-11-05.

Olaf Frohn d3-celestial constellation areas and Latin label positions, the spec-listed BSD-3-Clause fallback. https://github.com/ofrohn/d3-celestial/blob/master/data/constellations.bounds.json and constellations.json. All 89 polygons/label points (Serpens in two parts), unthinned J2000 vertices; numerical precision retained. Licence read first at https://github.com/ofrohn/d3-celestial/blob/master/LICENSE; full notice retained in Manual. Names checked against https://www.iau.org/IAU/Astronomy-FAQs/Constellations.aspx (CC BY 4.0). Fetched 2026-11-05. Reproducible packer: _scratch/sky-dome/fix_pack_data.py; raw downloads and manifest: _scratch/sky-dome/data/fix/.

Added stellar numerical distance facts: Rigel approximately 860 ly, NASA https://science.nasa.gov/universe/stories/quick-reads/discovering-the-universe-through-the-constellation-orion/ checked against de Almeida et al. 2022 https://arxiv.org/abs/2204.00372 (0.26 +/- 0.02 kpc). Antares approximately 550 ly, NASA https://science.nasa.gov/image-article/apod-2012-april-17-antares-and-clouds/ checked against Nature Astronomy, Turmoil at Antares (2017), https://www.nature.com/articles/s41550-017-0279-x, 170 pc (about 554 ly, consistent with the approximate 550 ly NASA value). No protected article prose or images reproduced. Numerical facts only, NASA public-domain factual material, no paper text or NASA/ESO images copied. Both marked approximate. Fetched 2026-11-05.

Seasons, original factual paraphrase checked against USNO https://aa.usno.navy.mil/faq/seasons_orbit and NASA https://science.nasa.gov/helio-and-you-seasons-on-earth-mars-and-beyond/. US Government factual material, public domain. Denver solstice one-day USNO API re-fetched 2026-11-05 at 39.7392,-104.9903, tz=-7, summer dst=true. Unchanged model daylight rounds to 14h59m / 9h21m; USNO rounded event differences 14h59m / 9h21m.

Sun distance: existing JPL Earth orbital elements https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/planets/approx_pos.html. Light time independently calculated from JPL numerical constants https://ssd.jpl.nasa.gov/astro_par.html au=149597870700 m and c=299792458 m/s; scale checked against NASA Sun Fact Sheet https://nssdc.gsfc.nasa.gov/planetary/factsheet/sunfact.html. US Government public-domain numerical facts, original computation, no copied text. Checked 2026-11-05.
